content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"JPQL (Java Persistence Query Language) Fundamentals"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Java Persistence Query Language (JPQL) is an object-oriented query language defined as part of the Java Persistence API (JPA) specification. It is designed to operate on persistent entity objects and their relationships rather than directly on relational database tables."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Concepts of JPQL"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Object-Oriented: JPQL queries use entity class names and property names instead of table names and column names."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Database Independence: Because it abstracts the underlying SQL dialect, JPQL queries work across different relational databases seamlessly."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Polymorphic Queries: Queries automatically return subclasses of the targeted entity, making it ideal for inheritance hierarchies."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Basic SELECT Queries"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"The simplest JPQL query selects all instances of an entity. Notice that we use the entity class name 'Employee' rather than the database table name 'EMPLOYEE_TBL'."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"SELECT e FROM Employee e"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Filtering Results with WHERE Clauses"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can narrow down results using a WHERE clause. JPQL supports standard comparison operators, logical operators (AND, OR, NOT), and named parameters to prevent SQL injection."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"SELECT e FROM Employee e WHERE e.department = :deptName AND e.salary > :minSalary"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Executing JPQL in Java"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"To execute a JPQL query in your application, you use the EntityManager interface to create a TypedQuery instance, set any defined parameters, and retrieve the results."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"TypedQuery<Employee> query = em.createQuery(\"SELECT e FROM Employee e WHERE e.department = :deptName\", Employee.class);\nquery.setParameter(\"deptName\", \"Engineering\");\nList<Employee> employees = query.getResultList();"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering JPQL is essential for building efficient, database-agnostic enterprise Java applications using JPA. By focusing on objects rather than tables, developers can write cleaner and more maintainable data-access logic."}]
